hints.title: Replace the logarithms with variables
hints.body: The separate logarithms require x>0 and y>0. Put X=log3(x) and Y=log3(y). The equations become X+2Y=1 and XY=−3.
hints.recap: Logarithm laws convert the system into algebra.
hints.pitfall: The new variables <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math> can be negative although <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> must be positive.
hints.pause: Eliminate Y using the linear equation.

recall.reminder: Combine product and power logarithms only on their allowed positive domains.

hints.title: Solve the quadratic in X
hints.recap: The quadratic factors as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: The requested values are x, not X.
hints.pause: Find both logarithmic values before converting back.

recall.reminder: Solve every quadratic branch before applying the original-variable definition.

hints.title: Recover and add the original values
hints.body: Recover the original variable by exponentiating each logarithmic solution in base 3. Check the corresponding second variable is allowed, then add the original values.
hints.recap: Negative logarithms give positive fractional values.
hints.pitfall: The sum of X-values does not equal the sum of x-values.
hints.pause: Calculate both original x-values and form their sum.

recall.reminder: Exponentiate the logarithmic variable to recover the original positive input.

solution:
Let X=log3(x) and Y=log3(y). The equations are X+2Y=1 and XY=−3. Substitution Y=1−X2 gives X2−X−6=0, hence X=3 or X=−2.

Therefore x=27 or x=19. In both cases the corresponding y=3Y is positive, so both are valid. Their sum is 27+19=2449.

Answer H: 2719.
knowledgePattern: Linearise logs then recover and sum original variable values
